rows.note: This is the all-purpose colloquial choice for wanting something or wanting to do something.

example.english: I wish to eat a bowl of wonton noodles.
example.jyutping: ngo5 soeng2 sik6 wun2 wan4 tan1 min6

rows.note: This is the all-purpose noun for a desired outcome or personal wish, especially in neutral contexts.

example.english: My wish is to have a home of my own.
example.traditional: 我嘅願望係有一間屬於自己嘅屋。
example.jyutping: ngo5 ge3 jyun6 mong6 hai6 jau5 jat1 gaan1 suk6 jyu1 zi6 gei2 ge3 uk1

rows.note: Use this when the wish is chiefly a hope or expectation that something will happen.

example.english: I wish it wouldn't rain tomorrow.
example.jyutping: ngo5 hei1 mong6 teng1 jat6 m4 hou2 lok6 jyu5

rows.note: Use this for a deeply personal or cherished wish, rather than an ordinary preference.

example.english: Grandma finally fulfilled her cherished wish to take her granddaughter travelling.
example.traditional: 阿嫲終於完成咗帶孫女去旅行嘅心願。
example.jyutping: aa3 maa4 zung1 jyu1 jyun4 sing4 zo2 daai3 syun1 neoi5 heoi3 leoi5 hang4 ge3 sam1 jyun6

rows.note: Use this when expressing hope for a particular outcome, especially one that may be unlikely.

example.english: I wish it wouldn’t rain tomorrow.
example.jyutping: ngo5 hei1 mong6 ting1 jat6 m4 hou2 lok6 jyu5

rows.note: Use this for a wish as an item expressed or made in a magical or ritual context, as in 許個願.

example.english: On my birthday, I made a wish in front of the candles.
example.traditional: 我喺生日嗰陣對住蠟燭許咗個願。
example.jyutping: ngo5 hai2 sang1 jat6 go2 zan6 deoi3 zyu6 laap6 zuk1 heoi2 zo2 go3 jyun6

rows.note: Use this in well-wishes and greetings such as 祝你聖誕快樂 ‘wish you a merry Christmas’.

example.english: I wish you a happy birthday!
example.jyutping: zuk1 nei5 saang1 jat6 faai3 lok6
